title: Uniqueness of restriction across a depth-positive boundary
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, and $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose $N(V)$ is finite over $\mathcal O_L(V)$ for every affine open $V$. Suppose for every $y\notin U$ the stalk $N_y$ is finite and has depth at least one [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Then for every open $V$ the restriction map $N(V)\to (j_*(N|_U))(V)$ is injective, where $j:U\hookrightarrow L$.

source.place: Tags 0B3M, 05AR and 00LL; injectivity step of Tag 0E9I

proof.text: At a boundary stalk, an associated maximal ideal would force depth zero. The proof is implemented by the private depth_zero_of_maximal_associated: association implies a nontrivial module; Nakayama rules out maximalIdeal times M = M; every nonempty regular sequence in the maximal ideal is contradicted by the union-of-associated-primes criterion for zerodivisors. Thus the supremum defining depth is zero, contradicting the positive-depth hypothesis.

On an affine open W, if s and t differ, the affine associated-stalk detection lemma supplies y in W with an associated maximal ideal and unequal germs. The preceding argument puts y in U. Equality of their images under the adjunction unit is equality after restriction to W intersect U, by restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app. Applying the germ at y and germ_res_apply contradicts the unequal germs.

For arbitrary V and a point x in V, choose an affine open W containing x and contained in V, using the affine-open basis. Naturality of the unit carries equality of the unit images on V to equality of the unit images of the restricted sections on W. Affine injectivity gives equality on W; germ_res_apply gives equality of the germs at x. The sheaf section_ext theorem gives equality on V.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0B3M and 05AR, combined with the regular-sequence definition of depth and the associated-prime zerodivisor criterion (00LL)
